verdict: Deckers grew sales 3.5% to a record $1.5B as HOKA and UGG both rose, and a $46M tariff refund lifted margins and profit well beyond what sales growth alone would suggest.

kpis.label: Revenue
kpis.note: +3.5% YoY (+2.8% in constant currency — ignoring exchange-rate moves)

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: +27% YoY; about $0.28 of it came from tariff refunds (see one-offs)

kpis.label: Gross margin
kpis.note: vs 56.2% a year ago; about 3.1 points of the gain came from the tariff refund

segments.name: UGG
segments.note: Sheepskin boots and shoes — the larger brand this quarter as its autumn season starts. Net sales rose 3.5% to $786M, with a 61.2% gross margin (what is left after the direct cost of the products).

segments.name: HOKA
segments.note: Cushioned running shoes — the faster-growing brand. Net sales rose 6.8% to $677M, with a 59.9% gross margin.

segments.name: Other brands
segments.note: Mainly Teva sandals, plus the last sales of brands being wound down (Koolaburra's standalone business was phased out). Net sales fell 54% to $17M because of that phase-out.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Running stores and websites, marketing the brands, and the back office. Rose 6% to $506M, growing a little faster than sales.

otherDetail: Other income was $14M, net: $15M of interest income on the company's cash pile (including $3M of interest paid on the tariff refunds), less $1M of interest expense, plus a small amount of other income.

takeaways.title: Both big brands grew
takeaways.text: Net sales rose 3.5% to a record $1,481M. UGG grew 3.5% to $786M and HOKA grew 6.8% to $677M, while Other brands halved to $17M as Koolaburra was phased out. Wholesale sales rose 5.5% to $1,093M; direct-to-consumer sales (its own stores and websites) slipped 1.8% to $388M. International sales rose 9% and made up 44% of the total.

takeaways.title: Margins jumped — mostly a refund
takeaways.text: Gross margin rose from 56.2% to 60.5%. About 3.1 points of that came from a $46M refund of tariffs (import taxes) previously paid, booked as a cut to cost of sales. Even without it, underlying margins improved, and operating income rose 19% to $389M.

takeaways.title: Profit rose 17%, buybacks shrank the share count
takeaways.text: Net income rose to $313M from $268M, and EPS rose faster — up 27% to $2.31 — because buybacks cut the share count: Deckers repurchased $299M of shares in the quarter ($638M so far this year). It also raised full-year EPS guidance to $7.80–$7.95.

oneTimers: Deckers received $46M of IEEPA tariff refunds in the quarter — money back for import tariffs it had paid under a policy later unwound — plus $3M of interest on the refunds. The $46M was booked as a reduction in cost of sales and the $3M in interest income, adding about $0.28 to EPS after tax. It is a one-off: without it, gross margin would have been about 57.4% instead of 60.5%.
footerNote: Reports in thousands; figures are rounded to $M. Cost of sales is shown as $586M (exact $585M) and UGG as $787M (exact $786M) so the lines add up.
follow100Note: The $46M tariff refund sits inside cost of sales, as the company reported it.
